A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AIpparel research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison despite the title change and supplementary figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original garment-generation and editing experiments, quantitative comparisons, and ablations in Sections 4 and S3.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds a GPT-4V captioning comparison and a 73-participant preference study.

M1.justification: The LLaVA-1.5-7B backbone, sewing-pattern tokenizer, regression heads, positional embeddings, and combined cross-entropy/regression objective remain unchanged. The added GPT-4V check does not replace the documented GPT-4o annotation pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use GCD-MM, SewFactory, and DressCode data with the same garment-generation and editing tasks. The human study evaluates existing generation modes, and the captioning check revisits an existing garment example.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark tables retain the same SewFormer and DressCode variants. However, the new human study labels its comparator only as 'Baselines' in Figure S10, without identifying methods by generation mode, so comparator membership in this added comparison cannot be verified.

E3.justification: Section S3.7 adds a protocol involving 10 multiple-choice questions and 73 participants judging prompt alignment and realism. Section S1.1 adds a GPT-4V captioning check. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and reconstruction metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new captioning comparison in Section S1.1 and Figure S2 examines whether design-parameter-informed prompting retains its advantage with GPT-4V. Existing tokenizer, objective, LoRA, and regression-head-depth ablations are retained.

E5.justification: No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added. The new preference study reports point percentages without uncertainty estimates; its participant count describes the evaluation sample.

E6.justification: Figure S10 adds AIpparel preference rates of 92.6% for images, 72.5% for text, and 90.0% for editing. Figure S2 adds a GPT-4V caption example. Existing numerical tables and qualitative result images remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical sewing-pattern representation, tokenization definition in Equation 1, and training objective in Equation 2 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The central dataset, tokenization, multimodal generation, editing, and performance claims retain their scope. Describing AIpparel as a 'multimodal foundation model' replaces earlier terminology without specifying new capabilities or stronger performance claims.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion attributing caption fidelity to design-parameter context despite GPT-version differences. Section S4.1 also specifies inherited coverage limitations from body models based on healthy European and North American adults, extending v1's general body-type and style caveats.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, annotation prompts, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and baseline implementation details are retained. The project address and planned dataset release are unchanged; the new study does not supply additional reproduction resources.

R1.justification: The same 87 referenced works and related-work comparisons are retained. The foundation-model terminology does not substantively change the stated technical relationship to previous garment-generation or multimodal-model research.

P1.justification: v4 revises the title and several contribution statements, makes localized wording edits, and inserts short captioning, human-study, and dataset-bias discussions. The overall organization and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the caption comparison in Figure S2 and the preference bar chart in Figure S10. Existing supplementary figures and tables are renumbered or relocated, while their original visual content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added human preference evidence, GPT-4V captioning check, and specific population-bias discussion modestly strengthen validation and transparency. The gains are limited by the ten-question study's sparse comparator reporting, absent uncertainty estimates, and the caption check's single example. The underlying method and existing benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
